mainTopic: Which ornaments and garments a woman may wear outside on שבת: the עיר של זהב, the כלילא, belts, a cloak, and rings with and without a seal
overview: The amud finishes defining the עיר של זהב, a gold ירושלים crown like the one רבי עקיבא made for his wife. A ברייתא gives three views on wearing it on שבת: רבי מאיר says it is a משוי, the רבנן say it is a תכשיט but forbid it in case she takes it off to show it, and רבי אליעזר permits it because only an אשה חשובה wears it. Next, רב and שמואל argue about a כלילא (tiara), and the גמרא gives two versions of exactly what they argue about. A tradition in רב's name permits the כלילא, and a story shows רב identifying לוי, who taught in נהרדעא that it is permitted. Women in נהרדעא and מחוזא relied on that ruling. The גמרא then rules on a fancy belt (קמרא), two belts worn together, and a short cloak with or without straps. It returns to the משנה to define קטלא and נזמים. Finally, it infers that a ring with a seal is not a woman's ornament. That clashes with a משנה in כלים, and רבי זירא resolves the clash: our משנה follows רבי נחמיה, who judges a ring by its seal, while the משנה in כלים follows the רבנן.

steps.title: The golden ירושלים is like the one רבי עקיבא made for his wife
steps.stepSummary: This line ends the definition of עיר של זהב. It is the kind of golden ירושלים crown that רבי עקיבא made for his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the one that רבי עקיבא made for his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its explanation of what an עיר של זהב is. It gives a famous example: the gold crown רבי עקיבא made for his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the previous amud defined עיר של זהב as a 'ירושלים of gold', meaning a gold crown with a picture of the city on it. This line adds a well-known real example, so the learner can picture it. The story is that רבי עקיבא promised his wife this crown in return for the sacrifices she made so he could learn תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A city of gold': a gold crown or ornament with an image of ירושלים

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the last words of a definition that started at the end of the previous amud.

phrases.english: Like the one that Rabbi Akiva made for his wife.
phrases.notes: Refers to the story where רבי עקיבא promised his wife a 'ירושלים דדהבא'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the definition of עיר של זהב begun on the previous amud.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An עיר של זהב is a gold ירושלים crown, like the one רבי עקיבא made for his wife.

steps.title: A ברייתא with three opinions on wearing a golden ירושלים on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records three views. רבי מאיר says she is חייבת חטאת. The חכמים say it is forbidden לכתחילה but she is פטורה if she went out. רבי אליעזר says it is permitted even לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A woman may not go out wearing a golden ירושלים, and if she went out she must bring a חטאת. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say she may not go out, but if she went out she is exempt. רבי אליעזר says a woman may go out wearing a golden ירושלים even from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with three different rulings about going out into the street on שבת wearing an עיר של זהב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three levels here. The strictest is רבי מאיר: it counts as real carrying, so there is a full חיוב חטאת. In the middle are the חכמים: it is forbidden only as a precaution, so she is פטורה if she did it. The most lenient is רבי אליעזר: it is fully permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Rabbis taught': this introduces a ברייתא
Must bring a sin-offering. This is the penalty for an accidental real מלאכה on שבת
Exempt from a קרבן. It is still forbidden לכתחילה
From the start, permitted in the first place

steps.confusionAlert: 'פטורה' for the חכמים does not mean it is allowed. They still say 'לא תצא', she should not go out. Only רבי אליעזר permits it לכתחילה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא תֵּצֵא אִשָּׁה בְּעִיר שֶׁל זָהָב,
phrases.english: A woman may not go out with a city of gold,
and if she went out, she is liable to a sin-offering,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say: She may not go out,
but if she went out, she is exempt.
Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹצְאָה אִשָּׁה בְּעִיר שֶׁל זָהָב לְכַתְּחִלָּה.
phrases.english: A woman may go out with a city of gold from the outset.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לֹא תֵּצֵא אִשָּׁה בְּעִיר שֶׁל זָהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that עיר של זהב has been defined, the גמרא brings a ברייתא about its law on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three views: רבי מאיר says חייבת חטאת; the חכמים say forbidden but פטורה; רבי אליעזר says permitted לכתחילה.

steps.title: What is the basis of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what idea lies behind the three-way argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the root reason is for each of the three opinions. This line sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a challenge. It is a request to understand the reasoning. The answer will show that each opinion comes from a different way of seeing the crown: as a burden, as an ornament with a risk, or as an ornament with no risk.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In what do they disagree?' This asks for the underlying reason of a dispute

phrases.english: With regard to what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The idea that explains each of the three rulings.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the crown counts as a burden
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that an עיר של זהב is a משוי, a burden, so wearing it out is real carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds that it is a burden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי מאיר's view. He treats the crown as a load being carried, not as jewelry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wearing a real תכשיט counts as being 'dressed', not as carrying. If the crown is a משוי, then walking out with it is the מלאכה of הוצאה. That is why רבי מאיר makes her חייבת חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: A burden or load. Carrying it into the רשות הרבים is real הוצאה

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds it is a burden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to במאי קמיפלגי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To רבי מאיר, the crown is a משוי, so wearing it out is a real חיוב חטאת.

steps.title: The רבנן: it is an ornament, but she might take it off to show it
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold it is a תכשיט, so there is no חטאת. They still forbid it, because she may take it off to show a friend and then carry it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold that it is an ornament. Still, perhaps she will take it off and show it to someone, and come to carry it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the middle view. It is jewelry, so no real carrying happens, but the חכמים made a precaution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The crown keeps its category as a תכשיט, which is why she is פטורה. The ban is a גזירה: a woman proud of a special piece may take it off to show it. Then she may end up carrying it in her hand four אמות in the רשות הרבים.

keyTerms.meaning: An ornament. Wearing it is not considered carrying
Perhaps, lest. This introduces a rabbinic precaution
She takes it off and shows it
She will come to carry it

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold it is an ornament —
lest she remove it and show it,
and come to carry it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the answer, set against רבי מאיר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To the רבנן, it is a תכשיט, so she is פטורה. It is forbidden because of the fear of שלפא ומחויא.
steps.whyThisMatters: The fear 'דילמא שלפא ומחויא' is a key reason behind many of this פרק's limits on women's jewelry on שבת.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: only an important woman wears it, and she does not show it off
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר agrees it is a תכשיט, but he rejects the fear. Only an אשה חשובה wears such a crown, and she does not take off jewelry to display it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר holds: who usually goes out wearing a golden ירושלים? An important woman. And an important woman does not take off her jewelry to show it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי אליעזר's lenient view. The worry of the רבנן does not apply to the kind of woman who wears this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר accepts the רבנן's starting point that it is jewelry. He argues only about the precaution. Because the people who wear it are women of high standing, the concern that she will remove it and carry it falls away, so it is permitted לכתחילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose manner is it, who usually does this

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views. רבי מאיר says it is a משוי, so חטאת. The רבנן say it is a תכשיט, forbidden because she may take it off and show it. רבי אליעזר says it is a תכשיט worn only by an אשה חשובה, who does not show it off, so it is permitted.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer holds:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דִּרְכֵּהּ לְמִיפַּק בְּעִיר שֶׁל זָהָב —
phrases.english: Whose manner is it to go out with a city of gold?
An important woman,
and an important woman does not remove it and show it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: מַאן דִּרְכֵּהּ לְמִיפַּק בְּעִיר שֶׁל זָהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer by setting רבי אליעזר against the רבנן's precaution.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To רבי אליעזר, the fear of שלפא ומחויא does not apply to an אשה חשובה, so it is permitted לכתחילה.

steps.title: A new ornament: רב forbids a כלילא (tiara) and שמואל permits it
steps.stepSummary: A new topic begins. רב forbids going out with a כלילא, and שמואל permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: About a כלילא (a tiara-like ornament): רב forbade it and שמואל permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a different ornament, the כלילא, and records a מחלוקת between רב and שמואל. This sets up the discussion that follows next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the golden crown, the גמרא turns to another headpiece. רב forbids it and שמואל permits it. The next two steps give two versions of exactly which כלילא they argue about and why.

keyTerms.meaning: A tiara or diadem worn on the forehead

phrases.english: A tiara: Rav prohibited and Shmuel permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the עיר של זהב to a related ornament, the כלילא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב forbids going out on שבת with a כלילא, and שמואל permits it.

steps.title: Defining the argument: metal is forbidden, woven-with-metal is disputed
steps.stepSummary: Everyone forbids a כלילא made of metal. רב and שמואל argue about a woven כלילא with metal set in it: which part is the main one?
steps.simpleTranslation: With a metal כלילא, everyone agrees it is forbidden. They argue about a woven one (with metal in it). One master holds the metal is the main part, so it is forbidden. The other master holds the woven fabric is the main part, so it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the exact edges of the argument between רב and שמואל from the last step. It tells us which case they agree on and which case they argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is narrowed. A plain metal כלילא is forbidden by everyone. The only argument is about a mixed item, woven fabric decorated with metal. רב treats the metal as the main part, so it is forbidden. שמואל treats the fabric as the main part, so it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: A headband or crown-like ornament worn on the head
Woven fabric (here, set with metal decorations)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב and שמואל argue about every כלילא. In this first version, a plain metal one is forbidden by everyone. The argument is only about a woven one with metal in it.

phrases.english: One of metal, everyone
phrases.notes: A כלילא made fully of metal

phrases.english: does not argue that it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Both רב and שמואל forbid it

phrases.english: Where they argue is about one of woven fabric:
phrases.notes: Woven fabric with metal set into it

phrases.english: One master holds the metal is the main part,
phrases.notes: רב, so it is forbidden

phrases.english: and one master holds the woven fabric is the main part.
phrases.notes: שמואל, so it is permitted

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דַּאֲסִיר. כִּי פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the scope of the argument between רב and שמואל stated in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A metal כלילא is forbidden by everyone. A woven כלילא with metal is disputed: רב says the metal is the main part (forbidden), and שמואל says the fabric is the main part (permitted).

steps.title: רב אשי's lenient version of the argument
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says everyone permits a woven כלילא. They argue about a metal one. רב fears she will take it off to show it and then carry it. שמואל says only an אשה חשובה wears it, and she does not do that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי taught it leniently. With a woven כלילא, everyone agrees it is permitted. They argue about a metal one. One master holds: maybe she will take it off, show it, and come to carry it. The other master holds: who usually goes out with a כלילא? An important woman. And an important woman does not take off her jewelry to show it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different, more lenient version of the same argument. He moves the argument from the woven כלילא to the metal one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the argument is no longer about which part is the main one. It is about a worry. רב fears she will remove the ornament to show it off and end up carrying it in רשות הרבים. שמואל uses the same reasoning רבי אליעזר used for the עיר של זהב in step 6: only an אשה חשובה wears this, and she does not take off jewelry to show it.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches it in a lenient version
She takes it off and shows it to someone

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the same 'אשה חשובה' reasoning from the עיר של זהב argument appears again. Here it becomes the basis for שמואל permitting even a metal כלילא.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi taught it leniently:
phrases.notes: A second version of the argument

phrases.english: one of woven fabric, everyone
does not argue that it is permitted.
phrases.notes: Both רב and שמואל permit it

phrases.english: Where they argue is about one of metal:
One master holds: perhaps she will remove it and show it
phrases.notes: רב's worry

phrases.english: and come to carry it,
phrases.notes: Carrying it four אמות in רשות הרבים

phrases.english: and one master holds: whose way is it
phrases.notes: שמואל

phrases.english: to go out with a kelila?
An important woman,
and an important woman does not remove it and show it.
phrases.notes: So there is no reason to worry

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative, more lenient version of the argument defined in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woven כלילא is permitted by everyone. For a metal one, רב forbids it out of fear she will remove it and carry it, and שמואל permits it because an אשה חשובה does not remove jewelry to show it.

steps.title: A report that רב himself permitted a כלילא
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר בר חנה tells רב יוסף: 'You clearly told us in רב's name that a כלילא is permitted.' This fits רב אשי's version, in which רב also permits a woven כלילא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר בר חנה said to רב יוסף: You told us clearly, in the name of רב, 'A כלילא is permitted.'
steps.whatsHappening: A student reminds his teacher רב יוסף of something רב יוסף once taught. רב יוסף had quoted רב as permitting a כלילא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We were told that רב forbids a כלילא, yet this report says רב permitted one. That fits רב אשי's version in step 9, where everyone, including רב, permits a woven כלילא. The report carries weight, since רב יוסף (who had forgotten his learning because of illness) himself once quoted רב as permitting it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר בַּר חָנָה לְרַב יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar bar Ḥana said to Rav Yosef:
phrases.notes: רב יוסף had forgotten his learning because of illness

phrases.english: You explicitly told us in the name of Rav:
"A kelila is permitted."
phrases.notes: Fits רב אשי's version, where רב permits a woven כלילא

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אשי's version in step 9: רב permits a woven כלילא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement in step 7 that רב forbids going out with a כלילא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יוסף himself had explicitly quoted רב as saying a כלילא is permitted, so רב's position seems to be the opposite of what was stated.

steps.title: רב hears that a great, tall, limping man taught that a כלילא is permitted
steps.stepSummary: People tell רב that a great, tall man who limps came to נהרדעא and publicly taught that a כלילא is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רב: A great, tall man came to נהרדעא, and he was limping, and he taught: 'A כלילא is permitted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story. It brings another voice that permitted the כלילא, and it sets up רב's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a second source permitting a כלילא, taught publicly in נהרדעא. The visitor is described only by his looks: great, tall, and limping. That sets up רב's guess about who he is.

phrases.english: They said to Rav:
A great, tall man came to Neharde'a
phrases.notes: נהרדעא, the town of שמואל

phrases.english: and he limps,
and he taught: "A kelila is permitted."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ לְרַב: אֲתָא גַּבְרָא רַבָּה אֲרִיכָא לִנְהַרְדְּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another report of a ruling permitting the כלילא and opens a short story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A great visiting scholar taught publicly in נהרדעא that a כלילא is permitted.

steps.title: רב identifies לוי and works out what happened in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב realizes the visitor must be לוי. From that, he concludes that רבי אפס died, רבי חנינא became head of the ישיבה, and לוי had no one to sit with, so he came to בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Who is a great, tall man who limps? לוי. Learn from this that רבי אפס has died, and רבי חנינא now sits at the head. לוי had no one to sit with, and so he has come here.
steps.whatsHappening: רב first identifies the visitor from his description. Then he draws a chain of conclusions about events in ארץ ישראל from the fact that לוי came.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While רבי אפס headed the ישיבה, רבי חנינא sat outside it out of his own greatness, and לוי sat with him as a colleague. If לוי left, רבי אפס must have died and רבי חנינא must now be head. לוי did not want to sit under his equal, so he had no partner left and came to בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; conclude from this
He passed away (literally, his soul rested)
To sit with him (as a study partner)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of the רב–שמואל argument. In the first, metal is forbidden by everyone and they argue about woven-with-metal. In רב אשי's version, woven is permitted by everyone and they argue about metal. After that come reports that רב himself permitted a כלילא, and the story of לוי, who also taught that it is permitted.

phrases.english: He said: Who is a great, tall man who limps?
phrases.notes: רב asks this himself

phrases.english: Levi.
phrases.notes: רב's answer: it must be לוי

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַפָּס
phrases.english: Conclude from this that Rabbi Afes has passed away
and Rabbi Ḥanina sits at the head,
phrases.notes: Of the ישיבה in ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: and Levi had no one
to sit with,
phrases.notes: He used to sit outside with רבי חנינא

phrases.english: and so he has come here.
phrases.notes: To בבל

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן גַּבְרָא רַבָּה אֲרִיכָא דְּאִיטְּלַע — לֵוִי, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב reacts to the report in step 11 by identifying the visitor and drawing conclusions.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The visitor teaching that a כלילא is permitted was לוי. His arrival showed that רבי אפס had died and that רבי חנינא had become head of the ישיבה.

steps.title: Maybe רבי חנינא died instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's reasoning. Maybe it was רבי חנינא who died, while רבי אפס stayed as head, and that is why לוי left.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps רבי חנינא died, and רבי אפס stayed in his position as before. Then לוי had nobody to sit with, and so he came here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions how רב could be so sure who died. It suggests the opposite possibility: רבי חנינא died, not רבי אפס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 12, רב concluded that רבי אפס died and רבי חנינא took over. The גמרא points out that the same result (לוי coming to בבל because he had no study partner) would also fit if רבי חנינא had died. So רב's conclusion seems unproven.

keyTerms.meaning: He stays as he stood (remains in his position)
To sit with him (as a study partner)

phrases.english: But perhaps Rabbi Chanina died,
and Rabbi Afes stayed in his position as before,
and Levi had no one
to sit with him,
phrases.notes: Earlier, לוי sat outside the study hall with רבי חנינא.

phrases.english: and so he came here?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's deduction from Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's conclusion that רבי אפס died and רבי חנינא became head
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same facts fit the opposite scenario, so the deduction is not proven

steps.title: לוי would have accepted רבי אפס
steps.stepSummary: First answer: if רבי חנינא had died, לוי would have accepted רבי אפס's authority and joined the ישיבה, so he would not have left.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were true that רבי חנינא died, לוי would have bowed to רבי אפס's authority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first reason why the other scenario is impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי only stayed outside the study hall out of respect for רבי חנינא, who was also not inside. If רבי חנינא were gone, לוי would have had no reason to stay out. He would have gone in under רבי אפס and not left for בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: He would surely have submitted to him

phrases.english: If it were so that Rabbi Chanina died,
Levi, to Rabbi Afes,
would certainly have submitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the other scenario contradicts known behavior
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe רבי חנינא died and לוי left
steps.terutzMaskana: לוי would have joined under רבי אפס, so he would not have left

steps.title: רבי חנינא had to become head
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: רבי חנינא could not die without ruling, because רבי declared before his death that רבי חנינא would sit at the head, and a צדיק's decree comes true.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, רבי חנינא could not possibly fail to become head. When רבי was dying, he said: 'חנינא son of רבי חמא shall sit at the head.' And about צדיקים it says: 'You will decree something and it will be fulfilled for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second reason, based on רבי's last wishes and a פסוק, that רבי חנינא had to become head of the ישיבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא had stepped aside for רבי אפס, even though רבי had chosen him. Since a צדיק's word is fulfilled, רבי חנינא could not die before reigning. So it must be רבי אפס who died, and רב's deduction stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is impossible that he would not rule
Shall sit at the head (lead the ישיבה)
You will decree a word and it will be fulfilled for you (איוב כב:כח)

steps.whatToRemember: רב's deduction holds: רבי אפס died, רבי חנינא became head, and לוי came to בבל. So the visitor who permitted the כלילא was לוי.

phrases.aramaic: וְתוּ, דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא לָא סַגִּי דְּלָא מָלֵיךְ,
phrases.english: And furthermore, it is impossible that Rabbi Chanina would not reign,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי הֲוָה קָא נִיחָא נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַבִּי
phrases.english: for when Rebbi was dying

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: חֲנִינָא בְּרַבִּי חָמָא יֵשֵׁב בָּרֹאשׁ.
phrases.english: he said: Chanina son of Rabbi Chama shall sit at the head.
And it is written about the righteous:
"You will decree a word and it will be fulfilled for you, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא לָא סַגִּי דְּלָא מָלֵיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second answer to the challenge of Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a צדיק's decree and a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא may have died without ruling
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי's decree had to be fulfilled, so רבי חנינא reigned

steps.title: Twenty-four women in נהרדעא
steps.stepSummary: After לוי taught in נהרדעא that a כלילא is permitted, 24 women went out wearing one.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי taught in נהרדעא: 'A כלילא is permitted.' Twenty-four women with a כלילא went out from all of נהרדעא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the כלילא and tells what happened after לוי's public ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling had a real effect: women relied on it and went out wearing the כלילא on שבת. Only 24 came from the whole city, which shows how rare this jewelry was.

phrases.english: Levi taught publicly in Nehardea:
"A kelila is permitted."
Twenty-four kelilas went out
from all of Nehardea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the story about לוי to the כלילא ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כלילא is permitted, and women in נהרדעא acted on this ruling

steps.title: Eighteen women from one alley in מחוזא
steps.stepSummary: After רבה בר אבוה taught in מחוזא that a כלילא is permitted, 18 women wearing one went out from a single alleyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר אבוה taught in מחוזא: 'A כלילא is permitted.' Eighteen women with a כלילא went out from one alleyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second story of the same ruling, this time in the wealthy city of מחוזא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מחוזא was a rich trading city, so 18 women came from just one alley, compared with 24 from all of נהרדעא. The point is that the permission had wide practical impact, especially where people were wealthy.

keyTerms.meaning: A wealthy trading city in בבל

phrases.english: Rabba bar Avuh taught publicly in Mechoza:
"A kelila is permitted,"
and eighteen kelilas went out
from one alleyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story to Step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כלילא is permitted, as taught in מחוזא
steps.whatToRemember: In practice, the כלילא was taught as permitted, and women relied on it in both נהרדעא and מחוזא.

steps.title: A fancy belt is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב שמואל: a woman may go out on שבת wearing a קמרא, a fancy belt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב שמואל: a קמרא (fancy belt) is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new piece of jewelry, the קמרא, and rules that it is permitted. This sets up the next steps, which explain what kind of belt is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is short and does not say what the belt is made of. That gap leads directly to the two versions that follow.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav Shmuel:
A gilded belt is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the כלילא to a related ornament
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Going out on שבת with a קמרא is permitted

steps.title: First version: a woven belt, like a gilded cloak
steps.stepSummary: One version says the belt is woven fabric with gold. רב ספרא compares it to a gilded cloak, which is clearly a garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say he meant a woven belt. And רב ספרא said: it is just like a gilded cloak.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first explanation of what kind of קמרא is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the belt is mostly fabric, the gold is just decoration on a garment. A gilded cloak is worn as clothing, not carried, so the belt is permitted for the same reason.

phrases.english: Some say it refers to one of woven fabric,
and Rav Safra said:
It is just like a gilded cloak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the קמרא from Step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woven belt with gold is permitted, like a gilded cloak

steps.title: Second version: a metal belt, like a king's belt
steps.stepSummary: Another version says the belt is all metal. רב ספרא compares it to the belt of kings, which is also permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say he meant a metal belt. And רב ספרא said: it is just like the belt of kings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version, in which even an all-metal belt is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version goes further: even a belt made fully of metal is permitted. It is still worn like a belt, just as kings wear golden belts, so it counts as clothing and not as carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: The belt of kings (made of gold)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In the first, the belt is fabric with gold. In the second, it is all metal. Each version has its own comparison from רב ספרא.

phrases.english: And some say it refers to one of metal,
and Rav Safra said:
It is just like the belt of kings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative version to Step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even an all-metal belt is permitted, like the belt of kings

steps.title: רבינא asks about a fancy belt worn over a regular belt
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי what the law is if a woman wears a קמרא on top of a regular belt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: What is the law if she wears a fancy belt on top of a regular belt?
steps.whatsHappening: Just before this, we learned that a woman may wear a קמרא, a fancy belt. Now רבינא asks what happens if she wears it on top of another belt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A single fancy belt is a real piece of clothing, so it is permitted. The new question is whether a second belt, worn over the first, still counts as clothing or becomes something extra that she is carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, the student and colleague of רב אשי
A fancy belt, sometimes decorated with gold

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
A fancy belt on top of a regular belt, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the permission for a קמרא to a new case: a קמרא worn over another belt.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a קמרא worn over a regular belt still counts as clothing.

steps.title: Two belts means the extra one is a burden
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that this means wearing two belts, and nobody normally does that, so it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You are talking about two belts! People do not wear two belts, so the top one is a burden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question. Wearing two belts is not normal, so the top belt does not count as clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something counts as clothing only when people normally wear it that way. A second belt serves no clothing purpose, so it is treated as something she is carrying, which is forbidden on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: You are saying (used here to show surprise: 'you mean two belts?')

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי does not spell out 'it is forbidden.' His surprised reply, 'two belts?!', is itself the answer: the extra belt is not clothing, so it is a burden.

phrases.english: He said to him: You are talking about two belts!
phrases.notes: In other words, nobody wears two belts, so the top one counts as a burden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Forbidden. A second belt is not normal clothing, so it counts as a burden.

steps.title: A short cloak is permitted only if it has tying straps
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rules that a רסוקא (short cloak) is permitted if it has straps to tie it on, and forbidden if it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: This short cloak: if it has straps to tie it, it is permitted. If not, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a new ruling about a short cloak. It depends on whether the cloak has straps to tie it to the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With straps, the cloak is tied on firmly and works as a real garment. Without straps, it can easily slip off, and she might end up carrying it in her hands in a public area.

keyTerms.meaning: A short cloak, or a piece of cloth worn over the shoulders
Small straps used to tie it on

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: This short cloak,
if it has straps for tying, it is permitted,
and if not, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling by רב אשי on whether a garment counts as clothing on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A short cloak with tying straps may be worn outside on שבת. Without straps it is forbidden.

steps.title: What is the קטלא the משנה forbids?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ban on going out with a קטלא and asks what a קטלא is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And not with a קטלא.' What is a קטלא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the words of the משנה. It quotes the item קטלא and asks what it means, setting up the definition that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists ornaments a woman should not wear outside on שבת. Before the law can be applied, we need to know what each word refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: An item worn at the neck, mentioned in the משנה

phrases.english: And not with a katla.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: What is a katla?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the belt and cloak rulings and returns to explaining the wording of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word קטלא in the משנה.

steps.title: A קטלא is a small bib worn at the neck
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that a קטלא is a small bib hung from the neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a small bib hanging from the neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by defining a קטלא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know which item the משנה forbids: a small decorative bib hung from the neck. It is an ornament, so the ban is not because it is a burden.

keyTerms.meaning: A small bib or decorative cloth hung from the neck

phrases.english: A small bib hung from the neck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what a קטלא is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קטלא is a small bib hung from the neck.

steps.title: The משנה's נזמים are nose rings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the נזמים forbidden in the משנה are nose rings, not earrings.
steps.simpleTranslation: The 'נזמים' in the משנה are nose rings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defines the next word in the משנה's list, נזמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word נזם could mean an earring or a nose ring. The גמרא makes clear that the משנה means nose rings.

phrases.english: Nezamim means nose rings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues defining the items in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The נזמים of the משנה are nose rings.

steps.title: A ring with a seal is not a woman's ornament
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a ring without a seal and infers that a ring with a seal makes her liable, so it is not an ornament for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Nor with a ring that has no seal on it.' This implies that if it does have a seal, she is liable to bring a חטאת. So a sealed ring must not be an ornament.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה's exact words closely and draws a conclusion from them. This conclusion sets up the next move, where it will be tested against another source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if she goes out with these ornaments she is not liable for a חטאת. Since it specifies a ring 'without a seal,' it follows that a ring with a seal is different: she is liable. That can only be because a sealed ring, which men use to seal documents, is not jewelry for her but a burden.

keyTerms.meaning: A seal (an engraving used to stamp documents)
She is liable (to bring a קרבן חטאת)
An ornament or piece of jewelry

steps.whatToRemember: A plain ring is a woman's ornament: wearing it out is only rabbinically forbidden, with no חטאת. A sealed ring is a man's tool, so for her it is a burden and carries full liability.
steps.confusionAlert: 'חייבת' here does not mean merely 'forbidden.' It means she actually broke a Torah law of carrying and must bring a חטאת. Wearing the other items in the list is only rabbinically forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This inference, that a sealed ring is not an ornament, is the claim the גמרא is about to test against other sources.

phrases.english: Nor with a ring that has no seal on it.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: This implies that if it has a seal on it, she is liable.
This shows that it is not an ornament.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא יֵשׁ עָלֶיהָ חוֹתָם חַיֶּיבֶת אַלְמָא לָאו תַּכְשִׁיט הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item in the משנה and draws an inference from its wording.
steps.raayaObject: That a ring with a seal is not considered a woman's ornament.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording, 'a ring that has no seal on it,' read by inference (דיוק).

steps.title: A contradiction from the משנה in כלים about sealed rings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in כלים that lists a ring with a seal as a woman's ornament. This contradicts the inference just made from our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they raised a contradiction: Women's ornaments can become טמא. And these are women's ornaments: bibs, earrings, and rings. A ring counts whether it has a seal on it or does not have a seal on it. Nose rings also count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different משנה (from מסכת כלים) that seems to say the opposite of what we just learned from our משנה. That משנה says even a ring with a seal is a woman's ornament.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 27 we inferred that a ring with a seal is not an ornament for a woman, so she is liable for carrying it on שבת. The משנה in כלים explicitly says a ring 'whether it has a seal or not' is a woman's ornament. If it is her ornament, she should not be liable, so the two משניות clash.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they contradicted it.' This formula introduces a source that contradicts the one just discussed.
A seal or signet engraved on a ring, used for stamping

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה in כלים is about טומאה, not שבת. The גמרא uses it only for its definition of what counts as a woman's ornament. That definition is what matters for שבת.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
phrases.notes: Introduces a conflicting source.

phrases.english: Women's ornaments can become impure.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה in כלים.

phrases.english: And these are women's ornaments:
bibs, earrings, and rings,
phrases.notes: Here נזמים means earrings, since nose rings are listed separately at the end.

phrases.english: and a ring, whether it has a seal on it
phrases.notes: This is the key phrase that creates the contradiction.

phrases.english: or whether it does not have a seal on it,
and nose rings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference of step 27 that a sealed ring is not a woman's ornament.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from our משנה that a ring with a seal is not a woman's ornament.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in כלים explicitly counts a ring with a seal as a woman's ornament. That directly contradicts the inference.

steps.title: רבי זירא: the two משניות follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא resolves the contradiction. Our משנה follows רבי נחמיה, and the משנה in כלים follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי זירא said: It is not difficult. This one is רבי נחמיה, and that one is the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the contradiction by saying the two משניות reflect two different opinions. He will prove this in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה treats a sealed ring as not a woman's item, and that follows רבי נחמיה. The משנה in כלים treats every ring as a woman's ornament, and that follows the רבנן. The משניות are no longer in conflict. They simply follow different views.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This formula introduces an answer.
This one... that one. Used to assign each source to a different opinion or case.
A תנא whose view is cited in the ברייתא below

steps.confusionAlert: The first 'הא' refers to our משנה in שבת, which follows רבי נחמיה. The second 'הא' refers to the משנה in כלים, which follows the רבנן.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira said: It is not difficult:
this is Rabbi Nechemya, that is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: Our משנה follows רבי נחמיה. The משנה in כלים follows the רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different תנאים: each source follows a different opinion (מחלוקת תנאים).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות express one view, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה follows רבי נחמיה, who sees the seal as the main part of the ring. The משנה in כלים follows the רבנן.

steps.title: The ברייתא: does a ring follow its band or its seal?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the dispute. The רבנן judge a ring by its band, while רבי נחמיה judges it by its seal. The same applies to a yoke and its rods.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: If the ring is metal and its seal is coral, it can become טמא. If the ring is coral and its seal is metal, it is טהור. רבי נחמיה says it can become טמא. For רבי נחמיה used to say: With a ring, follow its seal. With a yoke, follow its rods.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי נחמיה and the רבנן really disagree about rings. רבי נחמיה treats the seal as the main part, and the רבנן treat the band as the main part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coral cannot become טמא, but metal can. The רבנן decide by the band, so a metal band is טמא and a coral band is טהור. רבי נחמיה decides by the seal, so for him a ring with a seal is essentially a sealing tool. That is a man's item, as our משנה implies. For the רבנן the seal is secondary, so even a sealed ring is still a woman's ornament, as the משנה in כלים says.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא. This introduces a supporting תנאי source.
Its rods, the pegs that fasten the yoke to the animal

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן say a ring is defined by its band, so even a sealed ring is a woman's ornament (משנה in כלים). רבי נחמיה says a ring is defined by its seal, so a sealed ring is a man's sealing tool (our משנה).
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle ties the טומאה dispute to the שבת question. Whatever counts as the 'main part' of an object defines what the object is and who uses it.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: הִיא שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת וְחוֹתָמָהּ שֶׁל אַלְמוֹג — טְמֵאָה,
phrases.english: If it (the ring) is of metal and its seal is of coral, it is impure,
phrases.notes: The band decides, according to the רבנן.

phrases.aramaic: הִיא שֶׁל אַלְמוֹג וְחוֹתָמָהּ שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת — טְהוֹרָה,
phrases.english: if it is of coral and its seal is of metal, it is pure,
and Rabbi Nechemya deems it impure,
phrases.notes: In the second case, because the seal is metal.

phrases.english: for Rabbi Nechemya would say:
With a ring, follow its seal.
With a yoke, follow its rods.
phrases.notes: A parallel case: the fastening rods determine the status of the whole yoke.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא that proves רבי זירא's claim in step 29 that רבי נחמיה and the רבנן disagree.
steps.raayaObject: רבי זירא's claim that רבי נחמיה and the רבנן disagree about whether the seal is the main part of a ring.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about rings made of metal and coral, including רבי נחמיה's principle 'בטבעת הלך אחר חותמה'.
